messages.author: e32484f448e128cc
messages.subject: (some other) Parametric survival models?
parts:
Dear List,
Happy new Year! (not sure how far into the new year you're supposed to keep wishing people happy new year...)

I have a (possibly) very naive question; I know that you can do a few parametric survival models in INLA, which are all characterised by the tag inla.models()$likelihood$NAME$survival=TRUE. But is it not possible to use other data models (eg Gamma), which are already implemented in INLA but have this tag set to FALSE, to run a parametric survival model? And is there any plan of potentially extending the range of parametric survival models?

Thanks
Gianluca

messages.author: 9a89594e7fcb7aad
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] (some other) Parametric survival models?
parts:
On Tue, 2016-01-12 at 02:19 -0800, Gianluca Baio wrote:
> Dear List,
> Happy new Year! (not sure how far into the new year you're supposed
> to keep wishing people happy new year...)
To you and yours as well!

> I have a (possibly) very naive question; I know that you can do a few
> parametric survival models in INLA, which are all characterised by
> the tag inla.models()$likelihood$NAME$survival=TRUE. But is it not
> possible to use other data models (eg Gamma), which are already
> implemented in INLA but have this tag set to FALSE, to run a
> parametric survival model? And is there any plan of potentially
> extending the range of parametric survival models

the current support for survival is a bit messy and incomplete, and
somewhat unstructured. this is because we do not have any in-house
person doing/knowing(-well-enough) that field! I would be very keen to
have someone who knows this, going through it and clean this up in the
sense telling me what is 'wrong' and what to add and change. Ie take an
overall responsibility for the surv-models in the package (except
coding it up in C). Maybe also add a surv-HOWTO tutorial.

yes, there are many models which should make sense both in survival
data and in 'regression'. its possible to have both

family = "gamma"

and

family = "gamma.surv"

and do the selection there, or if the corresponding data-entry is a
inla.surv object, then do the change internally, so we can just use
family="gamma". 

If someone is interested, let me know...

H

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] (some other) Parametric survival models?
parts:
Hi Håvard,
Thanks --- as I've already mentioned to you, this is kind of an interesting topic in health economic evaluations, where parametric survival analyses are often a crucial part of the overall model. There are some guidelines on how and what models to test, but I think full Bayesian models are somewhat underdeveloped (from the practitioners' point of view) because "standard" MCMC implementations are generally slow and relatively complex to systematised... 

What you're suggesting sounds like a very interesting PhD project --- may be we can talk about this off-line?
BW
Gianluca

messages.author: 9a7eb279e53997eb
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] (some other) Parametric survival models?
parts:
1. I echo my support for developing a sound survival package with spatial component. 
2. I am very pleased to see spatial count models in INLA (poisson, NB, zero inflated etc..).  It would also be wonderful to develop some efficient way of doing multinomial models in INLA.  The mle version of this model (multinomial logit, multinomial probit, ordered logit etc..) is well-developed in Stata, Sas, SPSS and there are packages too in Bayesisn MCMC etc..  Many environmental, development, and health economists extensively use these models, but mostly without any spatial component (and quite rare in MCMC because of the time and complexity and the learning curve).    

Here is a very nice tutorial showing the use of R's mlogit function to estimate a  well-known environmental related choice problem.  https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/mlogit/vignettes/Exercises.pdf  There are many more applications in recreational field as well as in development and health economics.  (e.g., types of technology adoption, mode of transportation choices, decision to choose health insurance options, migration and recreation  decision, school choice so on...),  It would be wonderful to add some spatial component to this field of study (INLA's strength). 


Alok
